title: Wreck and Passage
premise: Hazel Joubert, a bush pilot who has spent a decade keeping her name off every registry in the territory, agrees to carry a dying prospector named Amos Vane to the coast hospital. In exchange for the flight, he gives her a chart marking a wrecked supply ship in the tidal flats—cargo enough to buy a new life, and proof that Hazel's own father, long presumed dead, was aboard when it went down. When word of the wreck leaks, a salvage fleet backed by the man who falsified her father's death record races them to the site. Over six tides before the concession permits expire, Hazel must choose between the anonymity she built and the identity she buried, flying impossible weather and confronting the salvage boss who knows exactly who she is. The story ends with Hazel claiming both the wreck and her real name, letting the salvage fleet take the cargo while she takes the truth—and finally landing somewhere she means to stay.
about_author: Elodie Ashgrove is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher who spent seven years in coastal aviation towns listening to pilots trade stories over bad coffee. She writes adventure fiction about people whose survival depends on machines, weather, and the lies they tell themselves.

chapters.title: Freight and Rumors
chapters.summary: Hazel flies medicine, mail, and gossip into remote camps, establishing her careful invisibility—no fixed address, no legal trail. A routine delivery to Amos Vane's claim reveals him feverish and failing. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the quiet loneliness of a life built on not being found.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Amos begs Hazel to fly him out tonight, against weather and regulations, offering payment she refuses until he mentions her father's name—a name she hasn't spoken in ten years. She agrees to fly at dawn. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the past cracking through the present like ice underfoot.

chapters.title: Six Hours of Storm
chapters.summary: A harrowing night flight through a front that nearly kills them both; Hazel lands on a logging road with a shredded wingtip and a passenger barely alive. In the ambulance bay, Amos presses a oilskin-wrapped chart into her hands. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into obligation.

chapters.title: What the Chart Shows
chapters.summary: In a motel room, Hazel deciphers Amos's map: the Meridian Star, wrecked in the Sable Tidal Flats, carrying registered cargo and unregistered secrets—including a passenger manifest with her father listed as crew. POV: Hazel, with a flashback to childhood. Emotional beat: grief reopening as possibility.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Paper
chapters.summary: Hazel investigates the death record and finds it was filed by Corwin Brase, now head of Brase Salvage and Concessions—the same company bidding on the flats. She realizes someone wanted her father erased. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: cold anger replacing mourning.

chapters.title: Tides and Deadlines
chapters.summary: Hazel learns the concession permits expire in six tides; after that, anything on the flats belongs to whoever holds the next license—Brase. She begins planning a run to the wreck in her patched plane. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: fear giving way to resolve.

chapters.title: The Only Mechanic Who Owes Me
chapters.summary: Hazel trades favors for repairs in the coastal town of Pelican Narrows, where mechanic Ruthie Okafor notices the chart and warns her that Brase's scouts are already asking questions. POV: alternating Hazel and Ruthie. Emotional beat: the risk of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Scouts
chapters.summary: Brase's men find Amos's empty cabin and trace the medevac flight. Hazel spots their boat shadowing the channel and realizes she is no longer invisible. POV: Hazel, with a brief Brase-organization interlude. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Hazel makes her first run at low tide, locating the Meridian Star's exposed ribs but unable to land safely. She photographs the site and finds fresh boot prints—someone else has been here. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: hope undercut by dread.

chapters.title: The Boy on the Beach
chapters.summary: Hazel discovers a teenage stowaway, Teo, living off the flats after fleeing Brase's employ—he can identify the salvage fleet's schedule. Reluctantly she takes him in. POV: alternating Hazel and Teo. Emotional beat: reluctant connection; belonging offered before it's earned.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: With Teo navigating the channels, Hazel lands on sandbar gravel and reaches the wreck's hold, finding sealed crates and her father's personal effects—including letters addressed to her. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Reading her father's letters, Hazel learns he discovered Brase was running contraband under salvage permits and planned to testify—that's why the record was falsified. POV: Hazel, flashback-heavy. Emotional beat: understanding her father at last, and what silence cost.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Brase's lead vessel arrives early; Hazel and Teo hide the plane in a fog bank and watch the fleet begin surveying. They realize the fleet doesn't know the exact coordinates yet—Amos never gave them up. POV: Hazel and Teo. Emotional beat: a narrow, breath-held advantage.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Brase himself contacts Hazel by radio, revealing he knows exactly who she is and offering a clean identity, money, and immunity—if she hands over the chart and forgets her father. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: temptation measured against everything she's lost.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Hazel refuses and runs the flats under fire from Brase's patrol skiff, damaging her tailwheel and forcing a brutal open-water landing. Teo saves the chart from going overboard. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in metal, blood, and nerve.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Stranded on an island with a crippled plane, Hazel and Teo make repairs while she confesses the whole truth of her old name and why she ran. Teo admits he stole from Brase and fears being sent back. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: two invisible people choosing to be seen by each other.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: A storm accelerates the tide schedule; Hazel gambles on a night approach and reaches the hold one last time, recovering the manifest ledger that proves Brase's fraud—but the fleet's divers are closing in. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened into precision.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Pelican Narrows
chapters.summary: Back at the strip, Ruthie has been coerced into reporting Hazel's movements; Brase's men seize the ledger and detain Teo. Hazel escapes into the hills with nothing but the original chart and her father's letters. POV: Hazel and Teo. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the discovery of what still matters.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Climax: with permits expiring at high water, Hazel flies through the storm's ragged edge, forces Brase's flagship aground on a sandbar using her knowledge of the flats, and broadcasts the ledger's contents to every radio in the district before the tide turns. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: fury and clarity fused into action.

chapters.title: Concession
chapters.summary: Authorities arrive; Brase's permits are voided amid investigation, and Teo is released into Hazel's guardianship rather than returned to his former employer. The wreck passes into protected custody—not hers, and she finds she doesn't want it. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: victory without spoils, and relief in that.

chapters.title: Her Father's Name
chapters.summary: Hazel files paperwork restoring her legal identity and formally records her father's true cause of death, standing in a government office she avoided for a decade. Amos dies peacefully, having kept his promise. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief completing itself; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Wreck and Passage
chapters.summary: Months later, Hazel runs a small charter outfit out of Pelican Narrows with Ruthie and Teo, flying medicine and rumors again—but this time with her name on the hangar door. On the last page she flies Teo over the flats at low tide so he can see the wreck once, then banks home. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: belonging, finally chosen and kept.
